title: My Wiki Birthday: My Journey as a Volunteer with Wikimedistas de Bolivia
content: On September 23, my Wikimedia account turned three years old. Although I started out editing slowly and without really knowing what I was doing, now, looking back, I realize that my daily life is filled with wiki projects, wiki skills, wiki people, wikifications, wikirquinchos, and more—including organizing a party to celebrate Wikipedia’s 25th anniversary in La Paz city. And all of this has allowed me to see that, even though I sometimes feel we’re very constrained in this world—where there are many things we “must” do and few we can propose—this is a place that allows for creativity and offers me a universe of possibilities.

title: Wikiquote Nigeria Campaign 2026 – Voices of Africa
content:
Africa has a rich tradition of storytelling, literature, oral history, ideas, and cultural expression. Yet many African voices and quotations remain underrepresented in online knowledge spaces.‎‎ To help address this gap, the Wikimedia community in Nigeria launched Wikiquote Nigeria 2026 – Voices of Africa, a campaign focused on increasing the visibility and accessibility of African voices on Wikiquote.

The campaign commenced on 11 July 2026, bringing together contributors around a shared goal: documenting African quotations and making them accessible as part of the world’s free knowledge.

title: From Ternate, WikiRempah Begins Its North Maluku Expedition and Holds WikiLatih with Universitas Terbuka
content:
Traveling more than 3,000 kilometers naturally raises many questions. Will transportation be reliable? Who will we meet and interact with? What is the current situation on the ground? And many other uncertainties.

Whatever the circumstances, we decided to go. North Maluku holds a wealth of knowledge that we believe deserves to be shared with the public. Ternate was once the center of a powerful sultanate that played an important role across the Indonesian archipelago. Even after Indonesia declared independence in 1945, the Sultanate of Ternate formally joined the Republic only in 1950. This reflects the significant position and influence the Sultanate held at the time.

So why have activities in Ternate not been as frequent as those in other Wikimedia communities? One of the main reasons is accessibility and the high cost of transportation in Eastern Indonesia. Reaching Ternate still requires significant support. With support from the Rapid Fund Wikimedia Foundation, the WikiRempah team therefore initiated a series of Wikipedia training activities in the region.

title: Notes from the Incubator: Writing a Short Story Anthology for the Incubator Sundanese Wikibooks Project
content:
When it comes to Wikimedia projects, the first thing that usually comes to mind is writing encyclopedic Wikipedia articles with a rigid, neutral, and heavily referenced tone. However, the Wikimedia ecosystem actually offers a much broader space than that. One of the most fascinating experiences I’ve had recently was contributing to the Sundanese Wikibooks project.

Unlike Wikipedia, which strictly focuses on facts, Wikibooks provides a platform for creating textbooks, learning modules, and even anthologies. It was here that I decided to embark on a slightly different initiative: compiling an anthology of short stories, affectionately known in Sundanese as Carita Pondok (Carpon).

One aspect that makes this project so special and challenging is the current status of the Sundanese Wikibooks, which is still housed within the Wikimedia Incubator. For those unfamiliar, the Incubator is a nursery for new Wikimedia projects before they “hatch” and earn their own dedicated domain (such as su.wikibooks.org).

title: Celebrating Wikipedia’s 25th Anniversary Through Local Community Engagement in Tabora, Tanzania
content: On 15 January 2026, Wikipedia celebrated its 25th anniversary. To commemorate this milestone, the Wikimedians of Tabora community hosted a local celebration that brought together volunteers who participated both in person and virtually to learn, share experiences, and contribute to Wikipedia. Beyond marking the anniversary, the event also aimed to bridge content gaps on the Swahili Wikipedia and welcome new editors into the Wikimedia movement. For many attendees, this was their first time participating in an in-person Wikipedia event. Others were experienced Wikimedians who had been contributing for years, but everyone shared the excitement of celebrating 25 years of free knowledge. Throughout the day, participants connected with one another, exchanged experiences, and so much more.

title: From Open Knowledge to National Development: Representing Wikimedia Botswana at the UN Consultation
content:
On 5 August 2026, I had the opportunity to attend a United Nations consultation on the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2027–2031, representing the Wikimedia Community User Group Botswana. The consultation brought together stakeholders from government, civil society, non-governmental organisations, and other sectors to discuss how the United Nations system and national stakeholders can work together more effectively to support Botswana’s development priorities. For me, the experience was particularly interesting because it allowed me to look beyond Wikimedia as an open knowledge movement and think about how the work we do can connect with broader national development conversations.

One of the first things I learned was that the Cooperation Framework is essentially a plan for how the United Nations and Botswana can work together over the coming years. The discussions connected the framework to Botswana’s wider development priorities, including National Development Plan 12, Vision 2036, and the Botswana Economic Transformation Programme.

title: Warm Makassar, A Note on Collaboration Along WikiRempah’s Journey to Eastern Indonesia
content:
Ever since the Makassar meetup was first announced online, members of the Wikimedia Makassar Community have welcomed the initiative with remarkable warmth and openness.

Led by Sekar Jarwo Soekarno and Iripseudocorus, the Wikimedia Makassar Community succeeded in significantly increasing both participant attendance and the volume of contributions produced during the event, results that were clearly visible when tracked through our laptops.

It is no exaggeration to say that the enthusiasm of our friends in Makassar was extraordinary. Their energy was so strong that it could even be felt by Wikimedia communities from other islands. This included us in the WikiRempah team Ana_Ainina, Supardisahabu, and Sofi Solihah, who came from Java Island, Gorontalo, and Manado respectively.

Both the local contacts and participants responded enthusiastically and showed a strong willingness to work together in increasing contributions to Buginese Wikipedia, the Makassarese Wikipedia Incubator, and the Buginese Wiktionary Incubator.

This enthusiasm was apparent from the very beginning of the event. Participants arrived early and came prepared to take an active part in the activities.

title: Scholarship applications for Wikimania Santiago are now open
content:
What does “The Internet we want” mean to you? What impact have you had on the Wikimedia movement to date and what do you hope to contribute in the future?

These are just some of the questions in the scholarship application to attend Wikimania 2027 in Santiago, Chile. The application form is now live and will be open through the end of the day on October 31, 2026. Applications will be accepted in any language, although the three official languages for this year’s event are preferred – Spanish, Portuguese, and English.

Scholarships to Wikimania 2027 cover travel to Santiago, hotel accommodation, and registration for the conference, which will take place from August 18 to 21.

Successful scholarship applicants are expected to volunteer for at least 4 to 6 hours during the event, in addition to participating in conference sessions and activities. Each year, Wikimania scholars form connections and friendships with other scholars from around the world. They also report that volunteering as a scholar gave them a strong sense of teamwork.

title: Wiki Rookies: Daejeon in-person meetup
content:
From late July to early August, roads across Korea are traditionally packed with people heading off on vacation.

In early August, the Wikimedia community in Korea and neurodivergent participants also took a special kind of vacation of their own: a photowalk in Yeongwol.

Yeongwol is well known for its historic sites associated with King Danjong, as well as for the film The Man Who Lives with the King, which tells a story centered on him.

We’d like to invite you, our readers, to join us as we look back on our time there.

The day of our photowalk, August 1, fell during what was close to the peak of Korea’s summer heatwave.

Since most of our route involved outdoor activities, we first filled up on some refreshing makguksu before heading out.

The tangy flavors of Seoul-style makguksu, the rich meaty broth of Gyeongsang-style milmyeon, and the mild, delicate taste of Gangwon-style makguksu came together to create a whole new world of flavors: Yeongwol-style makguksu.

Our next stop was Cheongnyeongpo, the first place where Danjong was exiled after being demoted to the status of Nosangun.
snippet: From late July to early August, roads across Korea are traditionally packed with people heading off on vacation.
creator: Hyoin WMKR

title: Tech News 2026 – Issue 39
content:
Latest tech news from the Wikimedia technical community. Please tell other users about these changes. Not all changes will affect you. Translations are available.

Weekly highlight

  • All wikis will be read-only for a few minutes on Wednesday, 23 September 2026 at 14:00 UTC. This is for the datacenter server switchover backup tests, which happen twice a year. During the switchover, all Wikimedia website traffic is shifted from one primary data center to the backup data center to test availability and prevent service disruption even in emergencies. [1]

    • Updates for editors

  • The Growth team tested a new post-edit notice designed to encourage Temporary Account holders to register for a permanent account. The new notice replaced multiple dialogs and a simultaneous welcome notification with a single message highlighting the benefits of creating an account. The experiment increased permanent account creation from 1.94% to 3.66%, an 87% relative increase. The change will now be released to all wikis. [2]

title: She came for the books and became a Wikimedian
content:
Jyoti Chiring began editing Assamese Wikisource after retiring from a career in nursing. She is now an active Wikimedian. This blog post stems from the conversation I had with her, while we were roommates at WikiConference India 2026. I was meeting her for the first time there, and she was kind enough to share her story with me, which I promised her will I share with the world. 

Jyoti Chiring did not join the Wikimedia movement because of free knowledge, or the encyclopedia, or anything so abstract. She joined because of books.

She had known a neighbour sitting with a laptop, and they spoke often enough in person for her to take the freedom to ask her what she was doing with it.

“She said, ‘I am working in Wikimedia as a volunteer.”

Jyoti immediately decided that she wants to do this thing like her neighbour. She had just transitioned from a very busy nursing superintendent to a retired mother, and the stillness of her retired life was making her wanting to do more in life.
